subject: Unable to use last index of an array - error in ConfigureMCMC

messages.author: 5cbb81b42989bdf3
messages.subject: Unable to use last index of an array - error in ConfigureMCMC
parts:
Dear all, 

I am trying to build an observation model for Covid19 in Norway to estimate the unobserved number of infected individuals.

To estimate the growth rate of the epidemic I am using a semi-mechanistic approach. The infected individuals on day "i" is calculated as the sum of the infected individuals on all the previous days, times the discretized serial interval evaluated at the difference in days. To store this sum I need to loop over all the previous indexes for each value of i. The sum on the last day is multiplied with the growth rate to obtain the prediction for the next day. 

However, for some reason, I am unable to configure the model when I try to use the last column index of the variable "store_sum". The error happens after the model is defined and I use the command "configureMCMC(MOD1, monitors = monitor,thin=1e1)".  I don't get any error messages, R just goes into an infinite calculation and I have to force quit the application to continue. 
The model works fine if I use index i-1 in the sum instead. 
Why doesn't configureMCMC work when I try to use the last index of my sum? It should be well defined by indexes provided in my loops. Am I confusing Nimble through the way I specify the dimensions? 

A reproducible example is provided below.
Any help greatly appreciated. 

Best regards,
Magnus Nygård Osnes


library(nimble)
chooseR = c(rep(1,18), rep(0,22))
constant_list = list(N0 = 6, Nend =41,chooseR= chooseR)


#THIS WORKS

mod_test = nimbleCode({
  m ~ dgamma(0.5,1)
  Rt <- mu #Growth rate
  Rm <- mu*exp(-m) #reduced growth rate
  tau <- 5.72
  
  ym ~ dexp(1.0/tau) #Seed the beginning of the epidemic. 
  prediction[1:N0] <- ym #Learn infected 6 first days
  
  for (i in (N0+1):Nend) {
    store_sum[i-N0,1]<-0
    for(j in 2:i) {
      store_sum[i-N0,j] <- store_sum[i-N0,j-1]+prediction[j-1]
    }
    contribution[i] <- store_sum[i-N0,i-1]
    prediction[i] <- Rt*(chooseR[i])*contribution[i] + Rm*(1-chooseR[i])*contribution[i]
  }
})

test_inits = function() {
  mu = 2.4
  tau = 5.72
  ym = 1/tau
  m = 1
  list(mu = mu,tau=tau,ym=ym,m=m)
}


MOD1 <- nimbleModel(mod_test,constants = constant_list,inits =test_inits())
monitor <- c("store_sum", "contribution") 
mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(MOD1, monitors = monitor,thin=1e1)


#THIS DOESN'T WORK: The only difference is: contribution[i] <- store_sum[i-N0,i], instead of contribution[i] <- store_sum[i-N0,i-1]. 

mod_test = nimbleCode({
  m ~ dgamma(0.5,1)
  Rt <- mu #Growth rate
  Rm <- mu*exp(-m) #reduced growth rate
  tau <- 5.72
  
  ym ~ dexp(1.0/tau) #Seed the beginning of the epidemic. 
  prediction[1:N0] <- ym #Learn infected 6 first days
  
  for (i in (N0+1):Nend) {
    store_sum[i-N0,1]<-0
    for(j in 2:i) {
      store_sum[i-N0,j] <- store_sum[i-N0,j-1]+prediction[j-1]
    }
    contribution[i] <- store_sum[i-N0,i]
    prediction[i] <- Rt*(chooseR[i])*contribution[i] + Rm*(1-chooseR[i])*contribution[i]
  }
})

test_inits = function() {
  mu = 2.4
  tau = 5.72
  ym = 1/tau
  m = 1
  list(mu = mu,tau=tau,ym=ym,m=m)
}


MOD1 <- nimbleModel(mod_test,constants = constant_list,inits =test_inits())
monitor <- c("store_sum", "contribution") 
mcmcConf <- configureMCMC(MOD1, monitors = monitor,thin=1e1)

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Unable to use last index of an array - error in ConfigureMCMC
parts:
Hi Magnus,

Thanks for posting your question.

I haven't tracked down why the second case goes into possibly infinite recursion, but a workaround is to include "useConjugacy = FALSE" in configureMCMC.  Determination of conjugate relationships for sampling involves tracing algebraic relationships through deterministic nodes.  With very long sequences of deterministic dependencies, this can get bogged down.  In this case it might be a bug.

A couple of other points I noticed: If I follow, it looks like chooseR should be one element longer.  And there are no data in the model, so ym will just follow its prior.  I realize you might still be building up the ideas.

If the very many deterministic dependencies in this model become cumbersome, you could do all of the store_sum and contribution work in a user-defined function.

Let us know further questions.

-Perry
